title: Contact holdout raised response prediction scores by 0.128 in 1,622 selected input groups from one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested whether the validation unit changes prediction of movie responses from synapse positions. We linked a verified MICrONS anatomy table to Ding v1 activity by nucleus ID. The main sample had 1,622 targets, 15,133 contacts and 148 sources in one mouse. At a 20 micrometre scale, contact holdout gave mean skill -0.1412 and whole-source holdout gave -0.2694, relative to an equal-input mean baseline. The observed gap was 0.1281. An exact random-label risk identity gave a mean gap of 0.1293. The main source-holdout score had upper-tail global label probability 0.101. A repeated-contact subset had contact skill 0.3226 and source skill -0.1821. It had a small exploratory source-score excess, which did not pass a conservative correction across the planned sensitivity tests. Thus a positive contact score or a contact-to-source score gap alone does not establish useful spatial prediction for a new source. This is an independent mouse test of a prior leech validation result. One animal, selected inputs, copied soma labels, Euclidean distances and inherited anatomy processing limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, label draws, hashes and external-data retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Observed and exact random-label prediction scores for contact and source holdouts. Main sample: 1,622 targets in one mouse. The repeated-contact subset has 72 targets. Label ranges describe a fixed-circuit reference, not uncertainty across mice. Data credit: Ding et al. and the MICrONS Consortium (2025).
